subject: unexpected links in brm with family="categorical"

messages.author: b9400d58a0bfce63
messages.subject: unexpected links in brm with family="categorical"
parts:
Hi,

First, thank you for your work on this excellent R package! Two hopefully straightforward questions:

1) The problem I am encountering occurs when fitting multinomial models using family=categorical(link="logit") or family="categorical".  The basic issue is that when I specify a logit link function for the categorical error distribution, brm returns identity links. Consider the following example:

ir2 <- brm (Species ~ Petal.Length + Petal.Width + Sepal.Length + Sepal.Width,
           data=iris, family=categorical(link="logit"),
           prior=c(set_prior ("normal (0, 8)")), chains=1)

This returns the following (see bolded):
summary(ir2)

Family: categorical 
  Links: muversicolor = identity; muvirginica = identity 
Formula: Species ~ Petal.Length + Petal.Width + Sepal.Length + Sepal.Width 
   Data: iris (Number of observations: 150) 
Samples: 1 chains, each with iter = 2000; warmup = 1000; thin = 1; 
         total post-warmup samples = 1000
    ICs: LOO = NA; WAIC = NA; R2 = NA
 
Population-Level Effects: 
                          Estimate Est.Error l-95% CI u-95% CI Eff.Sample Rhat
muversicolor_Intercept      -22.34     22.54   -69.48    18.18        417 1.00
muvirginica_Intercept       -55.21     25.92  -106.25    -8.65        585 1.00
muversicolor_Petal.Length     7.77      3.50     1.25    14.49        370 1.00
muversicolor_Petal.Width     -0.51      5.16   -10.64     9.55        531 1.01
muversicolor_Sepal.Length     2.48      4.75    -7.11    11.85        445 1.00
muversicolor_Sepal.Width     -3.43      4.09   -11.58     3.89        467 1.00
muvirginica_Petal.Length     16.19      4.08     8.75    24.57        399 1.00
muvirginica_Petal.Width      11.43      5.49     0.80    22.55        597 1.00
muvirginica_Sepal.Length     -0.36      4.78    -9.59     9.13        374 1.00
muvirginica_Sepal.Width      -7.18      4.31   -16.19     0.48        454 1.00

Samples were drawn using sampling(NUTS). For each parameter, Eff.Sample 
is a crude measure of effective sample size, and Rhat is the potential 
scale reduction factor on split chains (at convergence, Rhat = 1).


This behavior seems strange, and I don't encounter such problems when fitting a binomial model using logit or probit links. Oddly enough when fitting a multinomial model to my actual data, brm returns a logit link for the first response category and identity for all the rest, and nothing I modify in the function call seems to change anything...

2) My second question pertains to the default priors for a multinomial model. From what I can find online, it seems like brm abstains from setting default priors when family="categorical". Is this correct? Sorry if I'm missing something obvious!

Thank you so much for the help!
Tom

messages.author: 6e3dd74b422c061b
messages.subject: Re: [brms-users] Re: unexpected links in brm with family="categorical"
parts:
1) This is just an issue with the output of summary. The link is correctly applied.

2) By default, there will indeed be "no" priors on the regression coefficients. Se also prior_summary(<your model>) and stancode(<your model>)
